_table: Unconditional notice to quit: statutory grounds (no cure right)
_note: grounds carries the controlling citation inline.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

AK.grounds: Alaska Stat. § 34.03.220(a)(2): substantial damage or repeat violation within 6 months

AL.grounds: Ala. Code § 35-9A-421(c): material falsification of rental application; criminal activity affecting health/safety

AZ.grounds: A.R.S. § 33-1368(A): material falsification, repeated noncompliance, criminal nuisance

CA.grounds: Cal. Civ. Proc. Code § 1161(4): waste, nuisance, illegal use, criminal activity (also pursuant to AB 1482 just-cause § 1946.2(b)(1) for at-fault grounds)

CO.grounds: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-107.5: substantial violation (drug/violent crime)

DE.grounds: Del. Code tit. 25 § 5513(a): material misrepresentation in rental application

FL.grounds: Fla. Stat. § 83.56(2)(a): intentional destruction, unreasonable disturbance, continued unreasonable disturbance

GA.grounds: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50: holding over (no statutory cure for breach; lease terms control)

HI.grounds: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 521-72: criminal activity, threats, intentional damage

IL.grounds: 735 ILCS 5/9-209 (rent) and § 9-210 (breach); criminal activity per local ordinances

KS.grounds: Kan. Stat. § 58-2564(b): material noncompliance is not curable (immediate termination)

KY.grounds: KRS § 383.660(2): recurring noncompliance within 6 months (URLTA counties)

MD.grounds: Md. Code, Real Prop. § 8-402.1: breach of lease (general); illegal drug activity (Real Prop. § 8-402.1(a)(1)(ii))

MS.grounds: Miss. Code § 89-8-13(3)(b): repeat violation within 6 months

MT.grounds: Mont. Code § 70-24-422(2): substantial damage, criminal activity

NE.grounds: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1431(4): violent criminal activity

NH.grounds: N.H. Rev. Stat. § 540:2(II)(c), substantial damage; § 540:2(II)(d), nonpayment after Demand for Rent (subject to cure)

NJ.grounds: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(c) (destruction), (n) (criminal conviction on/related to premises), (p) (drug activity), (q) (firearm)

NV.grounds: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 40.2514: material misrepresentation; criminal activity (3-day no-cure)

NY.grounds: NY RPAPL § 711(1)-(5) and lease grounds; lease default + holdover are unconditional in many forms

OH.grounds: Ohio Rev. Code § 1923.02, multiple statutory grounds; § 5321.17(C), substantial breach

OK.grounds: Okla. Stat. tit. 41 § 132(B): repeat violation within 6 months

OR.grounds: ORS 90.396: 24-hour no-cure for outrageous conduct (assault, drug manufacturing, etc.)

PA.grounds: 68 P.S. § 250.501(b): lease forfeiture grounds (lease must specify)

SC.grounds: S.C. Code § 27-40-710(c): prior breach within 6 months

TN.grounds: Tenn. Code § 66-28-505(g): drug/violent crime (no cure required)

TX.grounds: Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005: default if lease so provides; § 91.003 (intentional misrepresentation)

UT.grounds: Utah Code § 78B-6-802: nuisance, unlawful activity, criminal activity

WA.grounds: RCW 59.18.650(2): enumerated unconditional grounds (waste, nuisance, criminal activity, gang activity, four-or-more-late-payments)

WI.grounds: Wis. Stat. § 704.17(2)(b): repeat breach within 1 year

WV.grounds: W. Va. Code § 55-3A-1: nonpayment / breach; lease terms control
